_note: Hand-curated sky events. Nothing here is scraped and nothing here is computed: every row is a fact a human read on the cited page and typed in, and every row carries source_url plus verified_on. Rows whose verified_on is null are explicitly unverified and are labelled that way in the UI. Peak times are UTC. What the observer actually sees - radiant altitude, moon interference, distance to a festival - is computed in the browser from these rows, never stored here. See docs/adr/0008-sky-events.md.

events.name: Draconids
events.notes: Very slow meteors. IMO 2026 calendar: maximum October 9, 01h UT (solar longitude 195.4°, J2000); no enhanced rates predicted for 2026.

events.name: Southern Taurids
events.notes: 2026 is a minor Taurid resonant-swarm year. Low rate, but a high share of fireballs.

events.name: Northern Taurids
events.notes: Broad, shallow maximum; overlaps the Southern Taurids.

events.name: Orionids
events.notes: Halley's Comet debris; fast meteors. IMO 2026 calendar gives the maximum as October 21 at solar longitude 208° with no hour, and rates can hold for several nights around it; peak_utc is when the Sun reaches 208.0° (J2000).

events.name: Leonis Minorids
events.notes: Very sparse; listed so a stray meteor near Leo Minor is not mistaken for an Orionid.

events.name: Leonids
events.notes: Peak date approximate — verify against a current almanac before relying on it.

events.name: Geminids
events.notes: Peak date approximate — verify against a current almanac before relying on it. The strongest annual shower.

events.name: Great Basin Astronomy Festival

location.place: Great Basin National Park, Baker, Nevada

events.notes: Dates approximate: inferred, not published. The park page says only that the festival is held near the time of the new moon each September (2026: September 10). Check the park page for the current programme before driving.

events.name: Cedar Breaks night-sky programs
events.notes: Ranger-led programs on Friday and Saturday nights through September 2026.
